notes:
Clips no longer come out with the wrong thing on top. The camera area you draw could be stretched over the entire frame, and nothing stopped it. A box that covers everything tells Jolnova that the whole screen is the camera, so the top strip of the clip showed the whole game instead of the streamer — and if "remember this for this streamer" was ticked, every later clip from that person came out the same way. Boxes that big are now refused, with an explanation.

The layout you pick is the layout you get. The camera window offers four layouts, but only two of them ever reached the clip: choosing "Automatic" or "IRL / Chat" silently gave you the split game view anyway. "Automatic" now decides the same way recording does — split view when a game is on, whole frame otherwise — and "IRL / Chat" really is the whole frame.

Fixing the camera can no longer destroy the clip. The rebuilt clip used to be written straight over the original, so if anything went wrong mid-way the clip was gone for good — and it did go wrong, leaving empty files behind. Jolnova now builds the new clip beside the old one, checks that it is really a playable video, and only then swaps it in. If anything fails your clip is left exactly as it was. There is also a progress bar with the elapsed time now, so you can see it is still working.

There is a user guide. It is in the menu on the left: what Jolnova does, step by step, with pictures of the real screens, written for someone who has never seen it before. The section on fixing the camera is the one worth reading.

Updating actually installs now. Until this version the update downloaded, the app closed and nothing was installed, because the script that does the work waited forever for a process that never exits. It was also about to install the wrong way, which would have left you with a setup wizard instead of Jolnova.

Jolnova opens in the language you installed it in, instead of always starting in English on the first run. "Launch Jolnova" at the end of setup works again; it used to do nothing at all if an earlier copy had got stuck. The Save dialog now opens in front of the window rather than behind it. The old ReelJolt name is gone from the save folder, and your files move with it.

Good clips are no longer thrown away. When a recording was deleted while a clip from it was still being scored, the clip scored zero for speech and was rejected as "boring" — indistinguishable from a genuinely dull one. Recordings still being used are now protected, and a clip whose source has gone is skipped and said so plainly.

Subtitle templates: the one you are using is marked with a tick, and picking a template now sets the whole look instead of leaving pieces of the previous one behind.

Plans you assign by hand can count as revenue. Jolnova asks whether the money actually reached you; say yes and that plan's price is added to your monthly revenue, say gift and it is not. Anything left unmarked stays a gift, so the figure can only ever be too low, never inflated.
